prompt:
以下はある英語ニュースpodcast記事のFull Story・Point One・Point Twoです。
Point One・Point Twoそれぞれについて、以下6項目を判定してください
(それぞれPASS/FAIL)。

- qa_not_caveat_only: このPointが、研究上の限界・一般化上の注意・免責事項
  だけで構成されていない場合PASS(それらに加えて実質的な新しい内容がある
  場合もPASS。留保だけでPoint枠全体が終わっている場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_full_story_paraphrase: Full Storyの要約・言い換えに留まっていない
  場合PASS(Full Storyの中心的なlogic・結論を語彙だけ変えて繰り返している
  場合はFAIL)
- qa_not_other_point_paraphrase: もう一方のPointの要約・言い換えになって
  いない場合PASS
- qa_explains_why_it_matters: 「だから何なのか」を具体的に説明できている
  場合PASS(聞き手にとっての具体的な意味・示唆がある場合)
- qa_specific_not_generic: この記事のLedger固有の内容に基づいており、他の
  どんな記事にもほぼそのまま流用できる一般論になっていない場合PASS
- qa_adds_new_value: 新しい理解・解釈・意外性・具体的示唆のいずれかを
  実際に加えている場合PASS(Full Storyだけを聞いた場合と比べて、聞き手の
  理解が実際に深まっている場合)

reasoningには、判定理由を1〜2文の日本語で書いてください(特にFAILの場合は
具体的な理由を明記してください)。

【Full Story】
Travel in Japan may be changing, but not in the simple way that says sightseeing is out and slow travel is in.

Among younger people, especially men, surveys show a growing wish to travel at their own pace. They want time for personal interests and more control over their schedules.

A 2025 survey found that, among men aged 29 and under, solo travel and hobby-focused travel were two of the most popular styles. Each was chosen by about one in four people.

Another survey found a similar wish for freedom. About 90% of Japanese Gen Z respondents aged 19 to 25 said they wanted free time during an overseas tour. About 80% of them wanted half a day or more.

But the length of actual trips tells a different story.

Among people planning a domestic trip in the autumn, the average stay was about two nights, and the middle figure was also about two nights. In a separate survey, people were asked what they would do if they could take a full month off. The most common answer was a trip of about one week, chosen by about one in four people.

So, the wish for a slower and more personal trip is clear. But the available evidence does not show that young travelers have already moved to long stays. A tourism white paper also lists longer stays as a policy task.

【Point One】
There may be two different meanings of “slow.” One is staying longer. The other is deciding how to use your time. The free-time findings mainly show a wish for control inside the itinerary. A traveler could want a half-day for a personal interest even on a short, two-night trip. That means counting nights alone may miss an early change.

【Point Two】
The shift is not uniform across all young people. Men under 29 showed strong interest in solo and hobby-focused travel. Among women under 29, gourmet travel was chosen by about half, while visiting famous tourist sites remained high at about 45%. Solo travel was also the top travel arrangement for men aged 18 to 29. Age alone may not tell travel businesses what young customers want.

point_one.reasoning: 「slow」を滞在日数と旅程内の時間の使い方に分け、短期旅行でも自由時間への需要が表れるという解釈を加えている。単なる調査結果の言い換えではなく、滞在日数だけでは変化を捉えにくいという具体的な測定上・実務上の示唆がある。

point_two.reasoning: 男性のソロ・趣味旅行志向と、女性のグルメ・有名観光地志向を対比し、若者を年齢だけで一括りにできないという事業者向けの示唆を加えている。Full Storyにない女性の具体的な数値と性別による需要差があり、独自の新情報になっている。
